titleEn: Vancouver Neighbourhood Renovation Cost Comparison 2026: Kerrisdale vs. East Van vs. Kitsilano vs. Richmond
titleZh: 温哥华社区装修成本对比2026：Kerrisdale与East Van、Kitsilano与列治文
contentEn:
Vancouver neighbourhoods differ enormously in renovation cost — not just because of property values, but because of housing stock age, soil conditions, heritage designations, and whether you own freehold or strata. Reno Stars has completed projects in 14 Metro Vancouver municipalities and 30+ distinct neighbourhoods. This guide breaks down what a whole-house renovation actually costs in each area, and why.

Why Vancouver Neighbourhood Matters for Renovation Cost

Three structural factors drive renovation pricing more than any other:

  • Housing stock age — East Vancouver homes built 1930–1970 have plaster-and-lath walls, knob-and-tube wiring in some areas, and steel-pipe plumbing that must be fully replaced. Kerrisdale and Shaughnessy character homes from the same era require heritage consideration. Richmond and Delta new-build areas (1990s+) have modern mechanical systems that rarely need full replacement.
  • Soil conditions — The West Side of Vancouver (Kerrisdale, Dunbar, Point Grey, South Vancouver) sits on Vashon glacial till: stable, well-drained, minimal differential settlement. The Fraser River floodplain under Richmond, Delta, and parts of Surrey has variable silt and clay, requiring deeper footings for structural work. Clayoquit clay in parts of West Vancouver expands and contracts with moisture, adding cost to foundation work.
  • Heritage and zoning overlays — Vancouver's Heritage Register covers 2,400+ buildings. Homes on the Register or in Heritage Conservation Areas (HCA) require Heritage Alteration Permits (HAP) before any exterior change. HAPs add $2,000–$8,000 in fees and 4–12 weeks to permit timelines. This affects Shaughnessy, Kerrisdale, Strathcona, and parts of Kitsilano and Fairview.

2026 Whole-House Renovation Cost by Vancouver Neighbourhood

All figures are for a mid-range whole-house renovation on a freehold single-family home — new kitchen, 2 bathrooms, flooring, electrical panel upgrade, trim and paint, exterior refresh. Premium/luxury tier adds 60–120%.

Kerrisdale, Shaughnessy & Point Grey (West Vancouver Area)

Character homes from the 1920s–1940s. Many are on or adjacent to the Heritage Register. HAP required for any exterior alteration. Knob-and-tube wiring present in ~40% of pre-1940 homes.

  • Housing stock: 1920s–1940s character homes, plaster-and-lath, heritage overlays
  • Structural complexity: High — heritage considerations, older foundations
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $180,000–$320,000
  • Premium: $350,000–$550,000+
  • Notable costs: Heritage consultant $3,000–$10,000, HAP fees $2,000–$8,000, knob-and-tube replacement $8,000–$25,000
  • Permit timeline: 8–16 weeks when HAP involved

Kitsilano, Fairview & South Granville

Mix of 1950s–1970s apartment buildings, 1980s–90s condos, and character homes near Broadway. Most whole-house work is on townhouses and apartment units rather than single-family homes. Heritage HCAs exist in parts of Kitsilano near the waterfront.

  • Housing stock: 1950s–1990s, mix of freehold and strata
  • Structural complexity: Medium — strata approval process adds 4–8 weeks for major work
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $130,000–$240,000 (townhouse/apartment); $200,000–$380,000 (character home)
  • Premium: $280,000–$500,000+
  • Notable costs: Strata approval $1,500–$5,000 (engineering report often required), heritage review where applicable
  • Permit timeline: 6–12 weeks + strata approval

East Vancouver (Grandview-Woodland, Commercial Drive, Hastings-Sunrise, Renfrew-Collingwood)

The most diverse housing stock in Metro Vancouver — everything from 1910s Edwardian bungalows to 1970s post-and-beam homes to 1990s infills. High proportion of knob-and-tube and galvanized steel plumbing. Most affordable freehold renovation market in Vancouver proper.

  • Housing stock: 1910s–1970s, highest proportion of pre-1940 homes outside heritage areas
  • Structural complexity: Medium-High — unknown conditions in older homes, possible asbestos in homes built before 1990
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $140,000–$250,000
  • Premium: $260,000–$420,000+
  • Notable costs: Asbestos testing/abatement $2,000–$18,000, knob-and-tube $8,000–$25,000, galvanized pipe replacement $6,000–$20,000
  • Permit timeline: 4–10 weeks (no HAP in most East Van areas)

Mount Pleasant, Main Street & Riley Park

Mix of character homes, 1970s townhouse complexes, and newer infills. Mount Pleasant is a Heritage Conservation Area — HAP required for exterior changes on character homes. Significant number of character homes from the 1920s–1930s. Rapid development means construction crews are readily available but competitive.

  • Housing stock: 1920s–1970s, mix of character and mid-century
  • Structural complexity: Medium-High — HCA designations in Mount Pleasant, mixed housing age
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $145,000–$260,000
  • Premium: $270,000–$440,000+
  • Notable costs: HAP $2,000–$8,000, heritage review, competitive trade pricing due to high renovation demand in area
  • Permit timeline: 6–14 weeks due to HCA

Richmond (Broadmoor, Seaforth, Steveston, Hamilton, Terra Nova)

Mostly 1980s–2010s construction on the Lulu Island Fraser River floodplain. Soil conditions require deeper footings for structural changes. Newer homes may still have Poly-B piping (see our Poly-B Replacement service). Freehold and strata mix. Steveston has heritage character near the village core.

  • Housing stock: 1980s–2010s, newer than Vancouver proper
  • Structural complexity: Medium — soil conditions for structural work, Poly-B in homes built 1985–2005
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $130,000–$230,000
  • Premium: $250,000–$400,000+
  • Notable costs: Poly-B replacement $12,000–$45,000 (if needed), deeper footings for additions $5,000–$15,000
  • Permit timeline: 4–8 weeks

Burnaby (Montecito, Capitol Hill, Brentwood, Metrotown, Edmonds)

Diverse municipality — Montecito and Capitol Hill have 1950s–60s character homes similar to East Van; Brentwood and Metrotown are dominated by strata high-rises and townhouses. Whole-house work in Burnaby splits between freehold character homes and larger strata townhouse renovations.

  • Housing stock: 1950s–present, very mixed
  • Structural complexity: Low-Medium — newer construction, newer mechanical systems
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $125,000–$220,000 (freehold); $110,000–$200,000 (strata townhouse)
  • Premium: $230,000–$380,000+
  • Permit timeline: 3–8 weeks

Surrey (Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey)

Metro Vancouver's largest municipality by land area. Housing stock spans from 1950s suburban lots in Cloverdale to newer infills in Grandview Heights. Significantly more affordable than Vancouver or Richmond for comparable scope. Growing Chinese-speaking population (40%+ of residents) means bilingual service availability is high.

  • Housing stock: 1950s–present, predominantly newer than Vancouver proper
  • Structural complexity: Low — newer construction, modern mechanical systems in most homes
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $110,000–$195,000
  • Premium: $200,000–$340,000+
  • Permit timeline: 3–6 weeks

North Shore (North Vancouver, West Vancouver)

West Vancouver is among the most expensive renovation markets in Canada — high property values, steep slopes in many lots requiring specialized engineering, and some of the oldest luxury character homes in Metro Vancouver. North Vancouver has more diverse stock including 1960s–80s townhouses and newer developments. Mountain proximity affects transport costs for materials.

  • Housing stock: 1930s–present, wide range — luxury character homes in WV, mid-century in NV
  • Structural complexity: High in WV (slope engineering, steep site access), Medium in NV
  • Mid-range whole-house cost: $160,000–$290,000 (NV); $280,000–$500,000 (WV)
  • Premium: $550,000–$1,200,000+ (WV luxury)
  • Notable costs: Slope engineering $15,000–$60,000, difficult site access, specialized trades premium in WV
  • Permit timeline: 6–14 weeks

Factors That Affect Every Vancouver Neighbourhood

  • Strata properties: If your home is a townhouse or apartment in a strata, factor in $1,500–$5,000 for engineering reports, strata approvals, and potential special levy — on top of the renovation cost. Strata approval alone can add 4–8 weeks to a project timeline.
  • Pre-1990 homes: Asbestos is present in floor tiles, vermiculite insulation, textured ceilings, and some pipe insulation in homes built before 1990. Budget $2,000–$18,000 for testing and abatement.
  • Electrical panel upgrades: Many Vancouver homes still have 60–100A service. Adding heat pumps, EV chargers, or induction ranges requires a 200A panel upgrade ($4,000–$8,000) in any neighbourhood.
  • Soil reports: For any structural addition or foundation work, a geotechnical report is required in most Metro Vancouver municipalities. $2,000–$5,000.

How to Use This Guide

If you are in the early research phase, these figures give you a realistic budget range to start from. The single most impactful step you can take is getting an in-home consultation with a contractor who has completed projects in your specific neighbourhood — conditions vary block by block in Vancouver. Reno Stars offers free in-home consultations across all 14 Metro Vancouver municipalities.

For neighbourhood-specific blog posts we have published: see our Strathcona heritage home guide, Richmond whole-house renovation guide, and Vancouver outdoor living space guide.

contentZh:
温哥华各社区的装修成本差异巨大——不仅仅是因为房产价值，还因为房屋年龄、土壤条件、遗产指定以及您拥有的是永久产权还是分契产权。Reno Stars已在14个大温城市和30多个不同社区完成了项目。本指南详细分析了在每个区域进行整体房屋装修的实际成本及其原因。

为什么温哥华社区对装修成本很重要

三个结构性因素比其他任何因素更能影响装修定价：

  • 房屋年龄 — 东温哥华建于1930年至1970年代的房屋有灰泥和板条墙，部分地区有老式电线系统，必须完全更换。Kerrisdale和Shaughnessy的特色住宅也来自同一时期，需要考虑遗产保护。列治文和Delta的新建区域（1990年代以后）的机械系统现代，通常不需要全面更换。
  • 土壤条件 — 温哥华西区（Kerrisdale、Dunbar、Point Grey、南温哥华）位于Vashon冰川堆积层：稳定、排水良好、差异沉降最小。列治文、Delta和素里部分地区的菲沙河冲积平原土壤多变，需要更深的地基来进行结构工程。西温哥华部分地区的Clayoquit粘土会随水分膨胀收缩，增加了地基工程的成本。
  • 遗产和分区覆盖 — 温哥华遗产登记处涵盖了2,400多栋建筑。遗产登记处或遗产保护区（HCA）上的房屋在任何外部变更之前都需要遗产变更许可证（HAP）。HAP会增加2,000至8,000加元的费用，并使许可时间延长4至12周。这影响了Shaughnessy、Kerrisdale、Strathcona以及Kitsilano和Fairview的部分地区。

2026年温哥华各社区整体房屋装修成本

所有数字适用于永久产权独立屋的中档整体房屋装修——新厨房、2间浴室、地板、电气面板升级、装饰和油漆、外部翻新。高端/豪华档次增加60–120%。

Kerrisdale、Shaughnessy与Point Grey（温哥华西区）

1920年代至1940年代的特色住宅。许多在遗产登记处或附近。任何外部变更都需要HAP。约40%的1940年前房屋存在老式电线系统。

  • 房屋年龄：1920年代至1940年代特色住宅，灰泥和板条，遗产覆盖
  • 结构复杂性：高——遗产考虑，较老地基
  • 中档整体房屋成本：180,000–320,000加元
  • 高端：350,000–550,000加元以上
  • 特殊成本：遗产顾问3,000–10,000加元，HAP费用2,000–8,000加元，老式电线更换8,000–25,000加元
  • 许可时间：涉及HAP时8–16周

East Vancouver（Grandview-Woodland、Commercial Drive、Hastings-Sunrise、Renfrew-Collingwood）

大温哥华最多样化的房屋库存——从1910年代的爱德华时代平房到1970年代的后现代住宅。超过40%的1940年前房屋存在老式电线系统和镀锌管道。这是温哥华市内最实惠的永久产权装修市场。

  • 房屋年龄：1910年代至1970年代，温哥华市中心以外1940年前房屋比例最高
  • 结构复杂性：中高——老旧房屋状况未知，1990年前房屋可能存在石棉
  • 中档整体房屋成本：140,000–250,000加元
  • 高端：260,000–420,000加元以上
  • 特殊成本：石棉检测/处理2,000–18,000加元，老式电线8,000–25,000加元，镀锌管道更换6,000–20,000加元
  • 许可时间：4–10周（大多数东温地区无HAP）

列治文（Broadmoor、Seaforth、Steveston、Hamilton、Terra Nova）

主要是1980年代至2010年代建筑，位于Lulu Island菲沙河冲积平原。土壤条件要求结构工程的地基更深。较新的房屋可能仍有Poly-B管道系统。

  • 房屋年龄：1980年代至2010年代，比温哥华市中心新建
  • 结构复杂性：中等——结构工程土壤条件，1985–2005年房屋Poly-B
  • 中档整体房屋成本：130,000–230,000加元
  • 高端：250,000–400,000加元以上
  • 特殊成本：Poly-B更换12,000–45,000加元（如需要），扩建 deeper footings 5,000–15,000加元
  • 许可时间：4–8周

北温哥华和西温哥华

西温哥华是加拿大最昂贵的装修市场之一——高房产价值、许多地块的陡坡需要专业工程、大温哥华最古老的高端特色住宅。北温哥华有多样化的房屋库存，包括1960年代至80年代的联排别墅和更新的开发项目。

  • 房屋年龄：1930年代至今——WV豪华特色住宅，NV中世纪
  • 结构复杂性：WV高（坡度工程、陡峭场地通道），NV中等
  • 中档整体房屋成本：NV 160,000–290,000加元；WV 280,000–500,000加元
  • 高端：WV豪华550,000–1,200,000加元以上
  • 特殊成本：坡度工程15,000–60,000加元，场地通道困难，WV专业行业溢价
  • 许可时间：6–14周（WV 8–20周）

影响所有温哥华社区的因素

  • 分契产权物业：如果您的房屋是联排别墅或公寓，分契审批需要额外增加1,500–5,000加元的工程报告和分契审批费用——在装修成本之上。分契审批本身可能使项目时间延长4–8周。
  • 1990年前的房屋：石棉存在于地板砖、蛭石保温材料、纹理天花板和一些管道保温材料中。为检测和处理预留2,000–18,000加元。
  • 电气面板升级：许多温哥华房屋仍使用60–100安培服务。添加热泵、电动汽车充电器或感应灶具需要200安培面板升级（4,000–8,000加元）。

Reno Stars是大温哥华地区的持证、担保装修承包商。所有项目均包含书面固定价格合同、500万加元商业综合责任保险、WorkSafeBC保险和3年工艺保证。申请免费咨询。
